findings.description: Under the sub-criterion 'Quality of the supervision, training and of the two-way transfer of knowledge', the primary supervisor is presented as a 'research associate' whose independent research track record is evidenced by a single recent paper. For an MSCA-PF, evaluators weigh the supervisor's seniority and demonstrated capacity to supervise a postdoctoral fellow to independence; the thin, single-item publication evidence for the primary supervisor is a shortcoming relative to the depth the criterion rewards.
findings.evidence: "Dr. Roland Hollós, research associate in the Department of Crop Production ... is the primary supervisor"; track record cited as "his own modelling line — the 2026 reimplementation and improvement of the Biome-BGC model".
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the supervisor's evidenced track record (e.g. supervision history, additional representative publications, grant leadership) to demonstrate senior capacity to deliver postdoctoral-level supervision, and make explicit how the two-supervisor structure compensates for the associate-level primary role.

findings.description: Under 'Quality and pertinence of objectives ... and the extent to which they go beyond the state of the art', the beyond-SOTA argument is framed conceptually as refusing four commonly conflated assumptions, but the section cites little specific competing literature to benchmark current practice. The ambition is asserted against a general characterisation of the field rather than positioned against named state-of-the-art approaches, which weakens the demonstration that the objectives go beyond the state of the art.
findings.evidence: "The project's ambition lies less in any single algorithm than in refusing four assumptions that are routinely conflated in crop-stress remote sensing".
findings.recommendation: Anchor each of the four 'refused assumptions' to concrete state-of-the-art references or established methods so the advance beyond current practice is benchmarked rather than characterised in the abstract.

findings.description: Under 'Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills', the Earth-observation/data-science half of the profile rests on non-publication evidence (an STSM, Erasmus mobilities, a UAV licence), with the remote-sensing publications recent and middle-authored. Although candidly acknowledged, this leaves the researcher's demonstrated competence in the modelling/EO strand — central to the action — comparatively lightly evidenced.
findings.evidence: "the three items touching remote sensing are recent and carry the researcher as a middle author, so the Earth-observation half of her profile rests on the STSM, the Erasmus mobilities and the UAV licence".
findings.recommendation: Reinforce the researcher's data-science/EO competence with any additional concrete outputs (datasets, code, presentations, first-author or in-preparation work) to show the developmental gap is narrow and the fellowship completes an already-substantiated trajectory.

findings.description: Under 'The magnitude and importance of the project's contribution to the expected scientific, societal and economic impacts', the section deliberately declines to state any quantified project-level impact target, anchoring magnitude only to external literature (an 8-30% water-saving band) and to application-domain scale statistics. While methodologically honest, the absence of any project-specific quantified magnitude claim can read to an evaluator as under-demonstrated magnitude of contribution.
findings.evidence: "It is deliberately a claim about methodological reach ... not a claim about immediate market penetration or a headline percentage of water saved."
findings.recommendation: Retain the honesty discipline but add bounded, project-controlled quantified magnitude indicators (e.g. target ranges for warning lead time, water-productivity measurement, expected reuse/adoption milestones) so the magnitude of the contribution is evidenced by the project's own metrics, not only by referenced literature.

findings.description: Under 'Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts ... dissemination and exploitation plan', the exploitation pathway's central operational evaluator (AgroVIR) rests on commitments that are declared assumed pending written confirmation — placement supervisor, working team, track-record framing and person-months. Because exploitation credibility hinges on this non-academic partner, the unconfirmed status weakens the credibility of the exploitation measures.
findings.evidence: Placement supervisor "Miklós Maróti" and AgroVIR track record are carried "as the operator's declared position, to be confirmed in AgroVIR's written placement letter".
findings.recommendation: Obtain and reflect written confirmation of the AgroVIR placement arrangement (supervisor, team, effort, operational track record) at grant preparation, and in the section frame the exploitation pathway so its credibility does not depend on figures still marked assumed.

findings.description: Under the dissemination measures, the scientific-publication ambition is modest for a 30-month postdoctoral fellowship ('at least two' peer-reviewed publications with a possible third). Relative to the data-rich five-season archive plus a novel prospective-validation dataset, this target may appear low against the dissemination expectations the Impact criterion assesses.
findings.evidence: "The action targets at least two high-quality peer-reviewed publications, with a possible third methods/application paper".
findings.recommendation: Consider raising or better justifying the publication target relative to the available datasets, and specify target venues/output types to demonstrate a credible, ambition-matched dissemination plan.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under 'Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks', WP3 — the prospective validation that sits on the project's critical path — depends on a single independent commercial farmer site whose written access is still assumed and whose identity is not yet stated, with only the Szentendre Skanzen route as a contingency that is itself subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability. The highest-value work therefore rests on the least-secured external dependency.
findings.evidence: "secured through the fellow's established professional relationship and deliberately kept as a collaborating validation environment"; "site identity is collected with the arrangement, not fabricated now".
findings.recommendation: Secure (or evidence progress toward) written field access before grant signature, and strengthen the contingency so the critical-path validation has a genuinely available fallback rather than one that is also conditional.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under 'appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages' and 'quality and capacity of participating organisations', the partner in-kind person-month contributions (ATK 2.5, ELTE 2.0, AgroVIR 3.0, MATE 2.4, Krumatic 1.5) are stated as operator-declared estimates pending written partner confirmation. The appropriateness-of-effort assessment thus rests partly on unconfirmed commitments from the participating organisations.
findings.evidence: "partner in-kind contributions that are stated as operator-declared estimates pending written partner confirmation".
findings.recommendation: Confirm partner effort in writing at grant preparation and, in the section, distinguish the fellow's confirmed 30 PM from partner in-kind figures clearly so the effort-appropriateness argument does not depend on unverified estimates.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under the work-plan structure, WP3 is led by 'the independent commercial-farmer validation site' — an entity that is neither a beneficiary nor an associated partner and whose access is not yet secured. Assigning work-package leadership to an unsecured, unnamed collaborating environment is structurally unusual for a single-beneficiary PF and could prompt an evaluator question about accountability for the critical validation package.
findings.evidence: "WP3 - Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation (lead: the independent commercial-farmer validation site)".
findings.recommendation: Assign WP3 leadership/accountability to the beneficiary (the fellow under HUN-REN ATK supervision) while retaining the farmer site as the validation environment, so the critical-path package has a clearly responsible lead within the funded entity.

revision_actions.action_description: Expand the primary supervisor's evidenced track record and supervision capacity, and make explicit how the two-supervisor structure delivers postdoctoral-level supervision despite the associate-level primary role.

Add bounded, project-controlled quantified magnitude indicators (lead time, water-productivity measurement, reuse/adoption milestones) alongside the referenced literature context to evidence the magnitude of contribution from the project's own metrics.
Secure written confirmation of the AgroVIR placement arrangement and reframe the exploitation pathway so its credibility no longer rests on assumed partner commitments.
Advance and evidence written field access for the WP3 validation site before grant signature, and harden the contingency so the critical-path validation has a genuinely available fallback.
Confirm partner in-kind person-months in writing and clearly separate the fellow's confirmed 30 PM from unconfirmed partner estimates in the effort-appropriateness argument.
Anchor each of the four 'refused assumptions' to named state-of-the-art references or methods so the beyond-SOTA claim is benchmarked rather than characterised abstractly.
Reinforce the researcher's data-science/EO competence with additional concrete outputs to show the developmental gap is narrow and evidenced.
Raise or better justify the publication target relative to the available datasets and name target venues/output types to demonstrate an ambition-matched dissemination plan.
Reassign WP3 leadership/accountability to the beneficiary while retaining the farmer site as the validation environment.
